about: Owner rules as code: each rule names the checks that enforce it and a violation fixture each check must fail on. check:rules (scripts/check-rules.mjs) enforces this file.

owner_words.quote: every page = frame + sections; Publisher never writes or designs

rules.note: Static class checks over the Studio app and Publisher page records; the hand-built StudioPage.tsx branches the audit found are W1/W2 fix units.

owner_words.quote: all views use Designer's shadcn components only

rules.note: The ds-only vitest (producer test) covers sections, frames, renderers and component-layer frames.

owner_words.quote: stock shadcn unmodified, tokens to shadcn vars

rules.note: Code-level gate: every pinned Designer candidate ships the vendored reference file plus only allowed hunks; an npm candidate ships only named re-exports of the package version package-lock.json resolves, and any other file it ships is that package's own file byte for byte.

owner_words.quote: DS exclusively shadcn plus trusted free registries

rules.note: Record-level gate: lineage must name a trusted manifest item; scans Foundry packages, not the consumer pins (consumer pins are R-SHADCN-STOCK).

owner_words.quote: visual to Designer, copy to Writer, assembly only to Publisher

rules.note: No check fails on a literal string in a Studio frame, section or renderer; the copy tests prove resolution only (W2 all copy through Writer).

owner_words.quote: consumer owns nav and routing data per publication

rules.note: Nav, commands and breadcrumbs must be Publisher projections of the pinned content map; the icon map overriding pins is a W-unit defect.

owner_words.quote: agents/<agent>/<slot-id>/ flat; grouping only in ia.json data

rules.note: No check fails when a legacy store (selection.json, library/, cells) is read or shipped (W3 CLI on flat slot folders).

owner_words.quote: every L3 is a slot, candidates are files, one pinned

rules.note: slot-resolve no-pin/multi-pin runs only inside clossys check, never from root check (W4 pin schema).

owner_words.quote: Studio previews the consumer workspace in the consumer brand; never greyscale

rules.note: No check fails when consumer brand assets point at Foundry files or a theme failure falls back to the Foundry theme.

owner_words.quote: read-only Studio; the card shows active state and links to the L3 route

rules.note: Class checks for the slot card and detail template; the read-only 405 API is covered by producer src tests.

owner_words.quote: Studio previews what cells produce, not file text

rules.note: No check fails when a slot detail falls back to a raw candidate-file-text table.

owner_words.quote: all layers link uses and used-by; DOM provenance

rules.note: usage-graph --check is freshness only; nothing compares slot.json uses with candidate imports or checks DOM provenance ids.

owner_words.quote: clossys verbs = brief, check, compile only

rules.note: No check runs the CLI verbs against the real consumer store, where they exit 2 (W3).

owner_words.quote: rules must become code, not prose

rules.note: Every check file is reachable from root check or test, and every rule has a check that fails on its fixture.

owner_words.quote: no temp solutions; delete shims, never extend

rules.note: No class check fails on a silent fallback (theme catch, unknown icon, newest-draft preview); only per-feature tests exist.

owner_words.quote: shadcn item, else a composition of pinned parts, else mark unneeded

rules.note: Every L3 slot is pinned or marked not-needed: check-slot-state lands with W4 and is not on this base.

owner_words.quote: the rendering itself is just the same deterministic plumbing that works everytime without llm token spend

rules.note: compile reads only ia.json, the content map, pins and pinned candidate files, offline, byte-identical across runs; the check is built on claude/compile-pure.

owner_words.quote: process driven by code and identifiers so that we decide which candidate goes in which slot

rules.note: Slot decisions (pin, not-needed) are written only by the clossys pin CLI; check:decisions fails on any hand-edited decision record (pin shape, candidate, hash, both, not-needed shape).

owner_words.quote: anything that is deterministic need to be process driven by code and identifiers

fixture_runs.expect: ^FAIL decide\.foreign-writer: workspace\.config \(decide\) owns clossys/clossys\.config\.ts, but scripts/rules/fixtures/R-PIPELINE-IS-CODE/repo-write/write-workspace-config\.mjs can write it

rules.note: Every pipeline step is a defineStep call; check:pipeline fails when a decide step's output can be written inside the repository by code outside its declared entry (a write that resolves outside the repository root, such as a scratch copy under os.tmpdir(), is not a repository write).

owner_words.quote: anything that is deterministic need to be process driven by code and identifiers

fixture_runs.expect: ^FAIL edge-ids: edge missing from the page: design\.hero->publish\.compile
^FAIL contain: the badge of step design\.hero .* overflows its node

rules.note: The Studio page /producer/pipeline draws graph.json only: check:pipeline-canvas renders it headless in the installed Chrome and fails unless the drawn node ids equal the step ids and the drawn edge ids equal the graph edges (from->to), with React Flow's pinned stylesheet and the generated --xy-* theme applied, no two node boxes (steps and lane labels) intersecting at the initial view in 1440x900, one label per lane, every step inside its lane's swim row, ranks left to right, every step title at 12px or more on screen at the initial view, the canvas filling the window's remaining height, the legend inside the viewport, every step's kind badge and title inside its node box, and (in the browser) a click on a step node or Enter on the focused step opening its sheet. The fixtures are recorded renderings: one drops an edge, one draws a kind badge past its node's right edge.

exemptions.reason: Render probe for a served published-site install (needs --url); site layout quality, not a Studio owner rule.
Producer server WebSocket upgrade transport test: infrastructure correctness, not an owner rule.
